headline: PM: July Movement's success belongs to the people, not any party
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that the mass uprising was driven by the people's desire for change, emphasizing that no single individual or political party can claim credit.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asserted that the success of the July mass uprising belongs entirely to the people of Bangladesh. Speaking at an event on Tuesday, he clarified that the movement was not the achievement of any single individual or political party.

The Prime Minister stated that the movement grew gradually and succeeded because the people genuinely desired change. He noted that while various claims have been made to mislead the public, the credit remains with the citizens.

Addressing reforms, he mentioned that his proposals had evolved into a 31-point plan. He criticized the previous 'fascist' government, claiming $16 billion was laundered from the country annually during its tenure.
He further alleged that the previous administration destroyed the banking, health, and agriculture sectors, leaving the population to suffer in a devastated state.

On healthcare, the PM highlighted the lack of kidney dialysis machines at the upazila level. He announced plans to install 50-bed units in most district medical colleges and 10-bed units in general hospitals within 3-6 months.
Additionally, he pledged that 10-bed dialysis centers would be operational at the upazila level within the next 2-3 years to improve accessibility to life-saving treatment.

headline_marked: 10 injured, including principal, as [[Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash]] at Alia Madrasa
headline: 10 injured, including principal, as Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash at Alia Madrasa
summary: Violence erupted between activists of JCD and Shibir in front of Dhaka Alia Madrasa, following earlier tensions at Jagannath University.
details: At least 10 people, including the principal of Dhaka Alia Madrasa, were injured during clashes between JCD and Shibir activists on Tuesday.
The violence broke out around 5:15 PM in front of the Madrasa, involving the throwing of bricks and stones and repeated chases between the two groups.
Tensions had been building since the morning, following a clash at Jagannath University over participation in the second anniversary of the July mass uprising.
Earlier in the afternoon, around 3:00 PM, another round of chases occurred, leaving several people injured and causing significant traffic congestion for nearly two hours.
Despite a temporary lull in the violence, the situation escalated again in the late afternoon, with clashes continuing into the evening.
caption:
10 people, including a school principal, injured in violent clashes between Chhatra Dal and Shibir activists in Dhaka.

Earlier in the afternoon, around 3:00 PM, another round of chases occurred, leaving several people injured and causing significant traffic congestion for nearly two hours.

Despite a temporary lull in the violence, the situation escalated again in the late afternoon, with clashes continuing into the evening.
